source: SIEVE authored supplement for function words and modern English

the.d: used to refer to a particular person or thing already known or identified

a.d: used before a singular noun to refer to one unspecified person or thing

an.d: the form of a used before a vowel sound

and.d: used to join words, phrases, or clauses

then.d: at that time or after that

while.d: during the time that, or whereas

whereas.d: in contrast with the fact that

since.d: from a past time until now, or because

so.d: to that extent, or for that reason

than.d: used to introduce the second part of a comparison

as.d: used to compare or to mean in the role of

of.d: belonging to, relating to, or coming from

to.d: in the direction of or toward

for.d: intended to be given to or used by

from.d: indicating the starting point or source

about.d: on the subject of, or approximately

between.d: in the space or interval separating two things

among.d: surrounded by or included in a group

through.d: from one side or end to the other

too.d: also, or to an excessive degree

really.d: in fact or to a great degree

even.d: used to emphasize something surprising or flat

still.d: up to now, or not moving

already.d: before now or earlier than expected

no.d: a negative answer or not any

hey.d: an informal greeting or call for attention

please.d: used to make a polite request

hmm.d: a sound expressing thought or hesitation

selfie.d: a photograph taken of oneself, usually with a smartphone

emoji.d: a small digital image used to express an idea or emotion

smartphone.d: a mobile phone with computer capabilities

website.d: a set of connected web pages

webpage.d: a document on the World Wide Web

email.d: electronic mail, or to send a message electronically

online.d: connected to or available through a computer network

offline.d: not connected to a computer network

wifi.d: a technology for wireless local networking

podcast.d: a downloadable or streamed audio program

streaming.d: delivery of media continuously over a network

blog.d: a personal website of regularly updated entries

hashtag.d: a word or phrase preceded by a hash sign as a topic label

meme.d: an image, phrase, or idea copied and spread online

screenshot.d: a captured image of a computer or phone screen

chatbot.d: a program that conducts a conversation with a user

blockchain.d: a distributed record of transactions grouped into blocks

drone.d: an unmanned aircraft or remotely controlled device

tablet.d: a flat portable computer with a touchscreen

smartwatch.d: a wearable computer with watch functions

earbuds.d: small headphones worn inside the ear

headphones.d: a pair of speakers worn over or in the ears

charger.d: a device for replenishing a battery

battery.d: a device that stores and supplies electrical energy

password.d: a secret string used to authenticate access

username.d: a name identifying a user of a system

login.d: the act of authenticating to a system

logout.d: the act of ending an authenticated session

download.d: to copy data from a remote system to a local one

upload.d: to copy data from a local system to a remote one

click.d: to press a mouse button or a short sharp sound

tap.d: to touch lightly or a light touch

swipe.d: to move a finger across a touchscreen

google.d: to search for information on the internet using Google

tweet.d: a short message posted on the social media service X

livestream.d: a real-time broadcast over the internet

cloud.d: a visible mass of water droplets, or remote networked computing resources

server.d: a computer or program that provides services to other computers

software.d: programs and operating information used by a computer

hardware.d: the physical parts of a computer system

algorithm.d: a finite sequence of steps for solving a problem

automation.d: the use of machines or programs to perform tasks

remote.d: situated far away, or a remote control

vaccine.d: a preparation that stimulates immunity to a disease

pandemic.d: an epidemic occurring across a large region or worldwide

lockdown.d: a restriction on movement for safety or security

telehealth.d: health care delivered remotely using telecommunications

electric vehicle.d: a vehicle powered by an electric motor

renewable energy.d: energy from sources that are naturally replenished

climate change.d: long-term change in global or regional climate

social media.d: online platforms for sharing content and interacting

machine learning.d: methods that let computers improve at tasks from data

artificial intelligence.d: computer systems that perform tasks associated with human intelligence

augmented reality.d: digital information overlaid on the physical world

deepfake.d: synthetic media that convincingly imitates a real person

misinformation.d: false or inaccurate information spread regardless of intent

disinformation.d: false information spread deliberately to deceive

fact check.d: to verify the accuracy of a claim

open source.d: software whose source code is publicly available

user interface.d: the means by which a person interacts with a computer system

natural language.d: language developed naturally by humans rather than designed for machines

command line.d: a text interface for entering commands

data structure.d: a way of organizing data for efficient use

source code.d: human-readable instructions that form a computer program

operating system.d: software that manages computer hardware and programs

search engine.d: a service for finding information on the web

web browser.d: a program for viewing web pages

touch screen.d: a display that responds to touch

screen time.d: time spent using a device with a screen

video call.d: a live audio and video conversation over a network

voice assistant.d: software that responds to spoken commands

large language model.d: a statistical model trained to predict text sequences

neural network.d: a layered network of numerical processing units

word sense.d: a particular meaning of a word in context

part of speech.d: a grammatical class such as noun, verb, or adjective

spelling error.d: a word written with incorrect letters or order

conversation context.d: information from earlier turns used to interpret a later turn

grounded world.d: a modelled situation whose objects and relations are explicit

unknown word.d: a token for which no declared lexical constraint exists

world model.d: an explicit representation of entities, attributes, and relations

constraint.d: a restriction that eliminates incompatible interpretations

interpretation.d: one possible meaning or action consistent with an utterance

ambiguity.d: the presence of more than one viable interpretation

i.d: the speaker or writer referring to themself

you.d: the person or people being addressed

he.d: a male person or animal already mentioned

she.d: a female person or animal already mentioned

it.d: a thing, situation, or animal already mentioned

we.d: the speaker together with other people

her.d: the object form of she, or belonging to her

mine.d: the thing or things belonging to me

yours.d: the thing or things belonging to you

hers.d: the thing or things belonging to her

ours.d: the thing or things belonging to us

theirs.d: the thing or things belonging to them

yourself.d: you, used for emphasis or as the object of your own action

himself.d: him, used for emphasis or as the object of his own action

herself.d: her, used for emphasis or as the object of her own action

itself.d: it, used for emphasis or as the object of its own action

ourselves.d: us, used for emphasis or as the object of our own action

yourselves.d: you, used for emphasis or as the object of your own action

themselves.d: them, used for emphasis or as the object of their own action

whose.d: belonging to which person or thing

which.d: used to ask for a choice among a known set

what.d: used to ask about a thing, situation, or identity

this.d: the person or thing near the speaker or just mentioned

that.d: the person or thing farther away or already mentioned

somewhere.d: in or to an unspecified place

all.d: the whole quantity or every member

either.d: one or the other of two

neither.d: not one and not the other of two

am.d: the first-person singular present form of be

is.d: the third-person singular present form of be

are.d: the present plural form of be and the second-person singular form

was.d: the past singular form of be

were.d: the past plural form of be and the past second-person singular form

being.d: the present participle of be, or a living creature

has.d: the third-person singular present form of have

had.d: the past and past participle form of have

does.d: the third-person singular present form of do

will.d: used to express the future or willingness

would.d: used for polite requests, conditions, or past habits

shall.d: used to express the future, obligation, or a suggestion

should.d: used to express obligation, expectation, or advice

can.d: to be able to or permitted to

could.d: the past form of can, or used for a polite possibility

must.d: used to express necessity or strong likelihood

ought.d: used to express duty or strong advice
